sections.history: Thevur (also Devur), near Kizhvelur in the lower Kaveri delta, lies about 16 km from Nagapattinam, 4 km south of Kizhvelur on the Nagapattinam–Tiruvarur road (sources place it in Tiruvarur district, some in Nagapattinam). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The village takes its name — 'the town of the devas' — from the sthala legend of the gods worshipping here, and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Deva Pureeswarar — also Devaguru Nathar and Kathalivanesar, 'lord of the plantain forest' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Madhurabashini, also Thenmozhiyaal, 'she of the sweet, honeyed words,' in her own shrine, with a Nandi and the parivara devatas.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the devas came to this place to worship Shiva and so be freed from the sin incurred in the slaying of an asura — in some tellings Vritra (Vruddhasura) — a deed that had stained even the gods. By their worship here they were cleansed, and from their presence the town is called Thevur, the city of the devas, and the lord Deva Pureeswarar. The name Kathalivanesar recalls a grove of plantain (kathali) that once stood here.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Kizhvelur include Thevur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Thevur the pilgrim stands where even the gods once came to be made clean. Before Deva Pureeswarar and the sweet-spoken Madhurabashini, the visitor finds a quiet delta shrine whose very name holds the memory of the devas' own worship — a small temple with a sky-wide legend.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thevur is about 16 km from Nagapattinam, 4 km south of Kizhvelur on the Nagapattinam–Tiruvarur road. Nagapattinam is the nearest major rail head, with buses via Kizhvelur and local taxis to the village.
